title: Corridor step 4 — BCCR bridges 500,000 CRC of its own reserves to the Hub
description: Lock spoke tCeBM, mint the mirrored Hub token against it. The position starts LOCKING; poll GET /api/v2/bridge/positions until it reads ACTIVE before doing anything with the Hub token.
notes: Gateway: BCCR (Banco Central de Costa Rica) Central Bank gateway, spoke-crc. Requires the central_bank realm role — note that /api/v2 uses lowercase unprefixed roles, while /api/v1 uses the ROLE_-prefixed ones; both namespaces coexist in the same token's roles array. Accepts a bearer token as well as the cookie (RequireAnyAuth). Send only amount: owner_bank_id comes from the session bankId claim and spoke_network / native_asset / mirrored_asset come from gateway configuration; all four exist in the request struct but are deprecated. Divergences verified in the delivered gateway: the documented 200 is really 201, and mirrored_asset comes back as the W-token ADDRESS, not the W-tCeBM_CRC symbol the platform's example shows, while native_asset is a symbol — one field, two kinds of value. This is one of the two chokepoints where the daily transfer limit is checked and deducted before value moves; exhausting it yields 422 TRANSFER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. The bridge-state vocabulary (LOCKING, ACTIVE, BURNING, BURNED, RELEASED, RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED) lives only in Go domain code; the PENDING/ACTIVE/CLOSED example in the platform document names two states that do not exist.
